verdicts.quote: "Sign in with Vercel is based on the OAuth 2.0 authorization framework… Access Token: A bearer token your application uses to call the Vercel REST API for the permissions the user grants."
verdicts.reason: A public OAuth2 flow exists to obtain user-scoped access tokens for the Vercel REST API, which fits the definition for primary_auth. ([vercel.com](https://vercel.com/docs/sign-in-with-vercel?utm_source=openai))

verdicts.quote: "To create an App… Navigate to your team's Settings… select Apps, and click Create" and "By default, anyone with a Vercel account can complete Sign in with Vercel for your app."
verdicts.reason: OAuth client apps (and thus working credentials) can be created self‑serve and used by any Vercel user without prior platform review; marketplace listing is a separate, optional review step. ([vercel.com](https://vercel.com/docs/sign-in-with-vercel/manage-from-dashboard))

verdicts.quote: "Browse all available REST API endpoints grouped by category. Access Groups 11 endpoints… Projects 33 endpoints… Feature Flags 28 endpoints… Marketplace 25 endpoints… Vercel CI 23 endpoints…"
verdicts.reason: The docs enumerate dozens of endpoint groups across most of the product surface, indicating broad coverage. ([vercel.com](https://vercel.com/docs/rest-api))

verdicts.reason: Vercel publishes and maintains an official, OAuth‑protected MCP server. ([vercel.com](https://vercel.com/docs/agent-resources/vercel-mcp?utm_source=openai))

verdicts.reason: With self‑serve OAuth apps and a broad REST API, Composio could ship an agent toolkit today without needing prior review; marketplace listing is optional and does not block building. ([vercel.com](https://vercel.com/docs/sign-in-with-vercel/manage-from-dashboard))
